A first stop before [Electric Basses Compared](bass-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the Rickenbacker is.
2. Learn how its pickups and controls make its sound.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Listen to famous tracks.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **4001** came out in **November 1961**; the **4003** followed in **1980**, almost the same but with a new truss rod for roundwound strings (Wikipedia, "Rickenbacker 4001").
- Two single-coil pickups: a "toaster top" at the neck and a "horseshoe" at the bridge, later "Hi-Gain" pickups (Wikipedia).
- A volume and tone for each pickup and a three-position switch (Wikipedia).
- Scale **33.5 in**, a little shorter than a Fender's 34 in. From 1968, a **Rick-O-Sound** stereo jack sends each pickup out on its own (Wikipedia; not modelled here).

## Its sound

- The bridge pickup sits very near the bridge: a bright, biting, twangy sound.
- Chris Squire used roundwound strings on his for "a bright, twangy bass tone" (Wikipedia).
- The neck pickup is far from the bridge: round and deep.
- Two single coils, so it can hum (whether its pickups cancel hum together: unverified; this page says not).

## The controls

The Rickenbacker's control area, drawn after the real one (positions approximate). Drag a knob (or use the arrow keys), then press a ▶ button. The sound is this site's physical model of a plucked bass string through these pickups and this wiring, into an amp; nobody has compared it with a real bass. The picture under the buttons shows the harmonics of the open A string (55 Hz) at the jack (bars) and the circuit alone (line).

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="ric4003" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;bridge&quot;}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Bridge.</b> The twangy, biting Rickenbacker sound.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="ric4003" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;neck&quot;}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Neck.</b> Deep and round.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="ric4003" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;both&quot;}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Both.</b> Fuller; some harmonics cancel.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="ric4003" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;both&quot;,&quot;vol1&quot;:5}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Both, neck volume at 5.</b> The blend leans to the bridge.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="ric4003" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;bridge&quot;,&quot;tone2&quot;:3}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Bridge, tone at 3.</b> The bite softened.</p></div>
```
